title: 2025 AMC 10B Problem 16
statement:
A circle has been divided into \(6\) sectors of different sizes. Then \(2\) of the sectors are painted red, \(2\) painted green, and \(2\) painted blue so that no two neighboring sectors are painted the same color. One such coloring is shown below.

How many different colorings are possible?

solutions.text: The six unequal sectors form a fixed cycle of \(6\) distinguishable positions, so we want proper \(3\)-colorings of a \(6\)-cycle that use each color exactly twice. There are \((3-1)^6 + (3-1) = 66\) proper \(3\)-colorings altogether. Of these, \(6\) use only two colors: choose the missing color in \(3\) ways, then alternate the other two colors in \(2\) ways. Another \(36\) have color counts \((3,2,1)\): choose the color used three times in \(3\) ways, choose one of the \(2\) alternating sets of positions for it, choose the color used twice in \(2\) ways, and choose its \(2\) positions among the other \(3\) in \(3\) ways. The remaining \(66 - 6 - 36 = 24\) use each color exactly twice. Therefore, the answer is D.
hints: The unequal sectors form a fixed cycle of \(6\) positions; you need proper colorings using each color exactly twice
A \(6\)-cycle has \(2^6 + 2 = 66\) proper \(3\)-colorings; remove those that do not use each color exactly twice
